name: Gorgon CO2 Injection
description: One of the world's largest CCS projects, separating CO₂ from the Gorgon LNG plant and injecting it into a deep saline formation beneath Barrow Island. It began injecting in 2019 but has stored far below its ~4 Mtpa design target — roughly 2.5 Mt in its first five years versus ~20 Mt expected.

name: Moomba CCS
description: Australia's first large-scale onshore CCS project, capturing CO₂ from the Moomba gas processing plant and injecting it into depleted gas reservoirs. Started injecting in late 2024.

name: Gippsland Basin CCS (SE Australia)
description: ExxonMobil/Esso-led project to repurpose depleted Gippsland Basin gas fields for CO₂ storage, serving industrial emitters in Victoria's Latrobe Valley and Gippsland region.

name: CarbonNet
description: Victorian government-backed CO₂ transport and storage network concept in the Gippsland Basin, aiming to connect Latrobe Valley industrial emitters to offshore storage.

name: Bayu-Undan CCS
description: Santos-led plan to convert the Bayu-Undan gas field, shared between Timor-Leste and Australia, into a large offshore CO₂ storage hub after gas production ends.

name: CNPC Jilin Oilfield CO2-EOR
description: China's first large-scale CO₂-EOR project, separating CO₂ from the Changling gas field and injecting it into the Jilin low-permeability oilfield for enhanced oil recovery since 2018.

name: Sinopec Qilu–Shengli CCUS
description: Sinopec's flagship CCUS project, capturing CO₂ from the Qilu refinery/petrochemical complex and piping it to the Shengli oilfield for enhanced oil recovery. First phase started in 2019, expanded toward ~1 Mtpa by 2021.

name: Yanchang CCUS
description: Integrated CCUS project at two coal-to-chemical plants in Yulin, capturing CO₂ for enhanced oil recovery in the Ordos Basin low-permeability reservoirs.

name: CNOOC Enping 15-1 Offshore CCUS
description: China's first offshore carbon capture, utilisation and storage project, reinjecting CO₂ separated from the Enping 15-1 oilfield into a nearby saline aquifer. Operating since 2023.

name: Guohua Jinjie CCS
description: Post-combustion carbon capture unit on a 600 MW unit of the Guohua Jinjie coal power station, capturing around 150,000 tonnes of CO₂ per year at a 90% capture rate since 2021.

name: Taizhou Power Plant CCS
description: Carbon capture on a coal-fired unit of the Taizhou power plant, capturing about 500,000 tonnes of CO₂ per year for utilisation and storage. Operating since 2023.

name: Tomakomai CCS Demonstration
description: Japan's offshore CCS demonstration, which met its 300,000-tonne injection target into sub-seafloor formations by 2019 before injection was suspended. Full-scale commercial expansion is under study.

name: Tangguh CCUS
description: Indonesia's first CCUS project, capturing CO₂ from the Tangguh LNG plant and reinjecting it into the Ubadari reservoir. Under construction with first injection targeted around 2026/2027 and long-term capacity up to ~15 Mtpa.

name: Abadi CCS
location: Abadi field, Masela Block, Arafura Sea
description: INPEX-led CCS integrated with the Abadi LNG development in the Masela Block, capturing CO₂ from the gas stream for reinjection into the Abadi reservoir.

name: Kasawari CCS
description: Petronas's first CCS project, capturing high-CO₂ gas from the Kasawari field and reinjecting it into a nearby saline aquifer offshore Sarawak. Under construction with first injection targeted around 2027.

name: Lang Lebah CCS
description: Planned CCS associated with the Lang Lebah high-CO₂ gas field development offshore Sarawak, part of Petronas's growing CCS portfolio.
